children: L'Oreal (LRLCY), the global beauty and cosmetics heavyweight, reclaimed the top spot in France by market capitalization, reaching roughly 203 billion and edging past LVMH (LVMHF) at about 201 billion. The valuation snapshot shows the shares at $86.11, with GF Value at $91.24, leaving the stock 5.62% below its estimated fair-value level.

The business underneath that valuation remains sturdy. First-half revenue reached 23.77 billion, up 5.8% on a reported basis, while operating margin widened 20 basis points to 21.3%. L'Oreal Luxe generated nearly 8 billion of sales and delivered adjusted like-for-like growth of 5.1%, giving the company another growth engine beyond its mass-market beauty franchises.

The market-cap lead over LVMH is tinyabout 2 billion, or roughly 1%so this crown could change hands quickly. What matters more is why investors are paying up for L'Oreal: repeat purchases, exposure across multiple price points and a distribution network stretching from pharmacies to prestige beauty counters. The picture adds another wrinkle. With the stock sitting 5.62% below GF Value, the market is giving investors a modest valuation cushion even as L'Oreal retakes the top of France's corporate leaderboard.

title: L'Oreal Takes France's Crown With a 203 Billion Valuation
